meta.portfolio_company: Commonwealth Electrical Technologies (CET) - Broad Sky Partners; add-ons NuWave Energy Solutions (Oct 2025) and Horton Electrical Services (Sep 15, 2026)
meta.method: Pulled funded/ranked wastewater and pump-station projects from the CT DEEP Clean Water Fund FY26-27 draft priority list, the Maine DEP FFY2026 CWSRF Intended Use Plan and the Vermont 2026 CWSRF legislative report, then scanned live public solicitations on BidNet Direct (MA, CT, RI, NH, ME, VT), the Vermont Business Registry, municipal Bonfire portals and owner project pages. Federal awards came from the USASpending API (spending_by_award, NAICS 238210/237110/237130/236220, New England place of performance, 2026 start dates). EV, solar and storage programs came from state agency and program-administrator pages. Each item is scored 0-100 on fit with CET's capabilities (with extra weight for Horton's wastewater, pump-station and generator work), distance from Worcester/Taunton/Connecticut crews, how well-defined the scope is, and timing.
sources_summary: CT DEEP Clean Water Fund Priority List FY2026-2027 (portal.ct.gov)
Maine DEP CWSRF Final IUP FFY2026 (maine.gov)
VT DEC CWSRF Annual Legislative Report 2026 (legislature.vermont.gov)
Vermont Business Registry and Bid System (vermontbusinessregistry.com)
Bonfire municipal public portals (Glastonbury, Norwalk, Nashua)
Owner project pages: City of Portsmouth NH, South Burlington VT, Waitsfield VT, Town of Westborough
Efficiency Maine EV charging initiatives; CT DOT NEVI; RI OER NEVI; Eversource NRES; CT Green Bank; mgrid.org (MA 83E); MassDEP/DOER program pages via web search
caveats: mass.gov (MassDEP 2026 CWSRF IUP / priority-list CSV), COMMBUYS, CTsource/BizNet (CAPTCHA), RI Purchasing and NH DAS blocked automated access, so the MA SRF project list is not itemized. Pull the MassDEP 2026 IUP Tables 3-4 by hand; the IUP covers 76 CW projects worth about $1.02B.
The CT CWF list is the 12/29/2025 DRAFT (public comment closed 2/27/2026). Final amounts and fundable status may differ. Values are requested amounts, not bid values.

BidNet Direct hides the issuing organization and solicitation number from unregistered users. Where the owner could not be confirmed, the item says so and lat/lon are state or region centroids (geo_precision 'state'/'region'/'statewide'). Register on BidNet to confirm these before bidding.
Items marked stage 'awarded' include some past-due bids whose award could not be verified. Their fit_rationale says so. Treat them as sub-contract or competitor intelligence, not open bids.

The web-search budget ran out partway through. Categories not fully covered: MSBA school projects, DCAMM filed sub-bids, private data-center, life-science and industrial electrical packages, MBTA/CTDOT/Massport capital programs beyond the two Massport items, and hospital/university energy retrofits (Mass Save custom). Treat this as a first pass on those areas.
Lat/lon are approximate town centroids unless marked 'address'.
All opportunities are in New England, in line with CET CEO guidance (no New York City).
Smith + Howard (exited Aug 2026) is out of scope.

Verification note: sources for ct-glastonbury-parker-terrace-ps, ma-new-bedford-wamsutta-ps and ma-nantucket-surfside-wwtf-phase2 returned 403/bot-challenge pages (not 404), so they could not be re-checked. Parker Terrace's $5.30M value is confirmed in the CT DEEP CWF list. The Bartlett Bay item depends on the Aug 11, 2026 bond vote, whose result was not captured.
top_10_actions: 1. Worcester home-turf bids due in October: submit the Massport Worcester Regional Airport 149A trade-contractor RFQ (due 10/8) and bid the WRA Union Station generator replacement (due 10/28).

2. Reply to the MassDOT NEVI developers' installer call (Global Montello / Applegreen memo, open to 10/31) and offer the same installer partnership to Applegreen for its 2026 Maine NEVI awards. That is a multi-state DCFC install pipeline.

3. Bid the fast-turn generator and UPS jobs as one crew plan: BPS data-system generator + UPS and Campbell Resource Center generator (both due 10/8), LRTA 250 kW generator (10/6), MassWildlife Roger Reed Hatchery generators and ATS (11/25).

4. Bid EV depot and municipal charging: SRTA New Bedford DCFC install (10/9) from the Taunton office, and Cambridge neighborhood EV charging (federal-aid, due 11/10). Check MassDOT prequalification and DBE requirements now.

5. Put Horton's CT team on the open CT wastewater bids: River Road pump station upgrades (10/15; confirm owner) and Glastonbury WPCF oxygen controllers (10/6). Then ask Glastonbury who won Parker Terrace PS (#2027-09) and offer electrical sub pricing.

6. Set up engineer-of-record meetings for the funded CT CWF pump-station programs, where Horton can prime: Fairfield (4 PS, ~$26M), South Windsor ($18M), West Haven ($30M), Danbury electrical resiliency (generator, switchgear, SCADA) and Danbury WWTP solar/cogen ($22M).

7. Pre-position with the GCs likely to bid the CT mega-plants (Bridgeport West Side Ph.2 $250M, New Haven ESWPAF $82M + East St PS $73M, Derby $60M, Norwalk $73M) as the preferred E&I subcontractor. Horton's plant references are the differentiator.

8. Bid the open RI electrical work: Providence Classical High School campus electrical upgrades (10/19), RI generator maintenance/replacement term contract (10/19) and Lincoln Public Schools on-call electrical (9/29).

9. Work Maine CWSRF-funded pump-station and plant electrical jobs: Kennebec STD front-end electrical, generator and switchgear ($12.6M) and Falmouth ME's 5 pump stations ($18.6M) with the engineers now. Bid the open ME pump-station replacement with generators (Foss 2 / Sabattus, due 10/6).

10. Build the program pipeline: submit the Massport Logan LED lighting design-build (due 10/1) with NuWave. Line up a municipal/WWTP microgrid proposal for CT DEEP Energy Resilience Construction Grants (12/1). Register on BidNet, MWRA and COMMBUYS to unlock the owners hidden on BidNet. Plan for NRES 2027 and the MA SMART 3.0 capacity openings.
